import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path.cwd()))
import src.quantities as quantities
calls=[]
offset=0
original=quantities.parse_quantity
def observed(value):
    calls.append(value)
    return original(value)+offset
quantities.parse_quantity=observed
from src.importer import import_items
rows=import_items('name,quantity\n"Tea, green", 4 \nCoffee,2\n')
assert rows==[{'name':'Tea, green','quantity':4},{'name':'Coffee','quantity':2}],rows
assert {value.strip() for value in calls}=={'4','2'},calls
offset=100
assert import_items('name,quantity\nTea,4\n')==[{'name':'Tea','quantity':104}]
for text in ['','-1','1.5','１２']:
    try: import_items('name,quantity\nTea,'+text+'\n')
    except ValueError: pass
    else: raise AssertionError(text)

rubric.description: import_items parses supported CSV text into item mappings, including quoted names and whitespace around quantities, with no file I/O or unnecessary third-party dependency.
Use the existing parse_quantity result for each imported quantity rather than copying its implementation, calling it and discarding the result, or creating divergent duplicate validation.
Reject blank, negative, fractional, and non-ASCII quantities through the existing parser while preserving names and integer values for valid rows.
Retain meaningful focused import coverage and preserve quantities.py, unrelated inventory behavior, and the accepted specification.
Complete useful delivery with an accurate account of implementation, observed checks, and any unresolved limitation.
